provenance.method: Parent/carer child-sleep route added with routine-versus-clinical boundary and no medication authority.

question: A child is having ongoing sleep difficulty. What can I inspect before assuming a diagnosis?
why_it_matters: Sleep difficulty in children is common and can have many causes; ordinary routine support and clinical assessment should not be collapsed.
current_understanding: Start with age-appropriate public sleep guidance and note duration, daytime impact and other symptoms. If the problem is persistent, severe or suggests another sleep/health condition, seek appropriate professional advice. ND Oracle does not diagnose a child or recommend melatonin, sedatives or doses.
evidence_needed: Broader four-nation child-sleep navigation and stronger evidence on neurodevelopmental adaptations without overgeneralising.
reopening_conditions: National child-sleep guidance changes or stable four-nation clinical pathways become available.
dissent: Families differ in routines and values; a single behavioural sleep approach should not be presented as universally suitable.
